text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.4% today as oil prices climbed on escalating Middle East tensions between Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia. Worries about potential supply disruptions in a region critical to global oil output pushed crude higher—US oil hit $96.24 a barrel and world oil reached $125.44, benefiting the company as an oil producer whose revenues rise when energy prices strengthen.

The stock's 12% gain over the past two weeks reflects a broader rally as geopolitical risk in the Middle East has mounted. The gap between US and world oil prices (nearly $30 a barrel) underscores how global supply concerns are driving the move—traders are pricing in real risk of disruption even as some offset from Russian diesel supplies remains uncertain.
